title: AI Daily Brief - 2026-06-15
tags:
  - applied-ai
---

## Today in One Minute

- OpenAI Academy has launched new "Applying AI at Work" courses, aimed at helping working professionals build practical AI skills.
- Google is rolling out new measures to fight AI-powered scams, combining product security, user education, and policy work.
- A Towards Data Science guide shows how Vision LLMs can read charts and diagrams inside PDFs, opening up better document Q&A for teaching materials and reports.

## What Happened

- OpenAI announced a fresh batch of free OpenAI Academy courses focused on applying AI in everyday work tasks, including practical use cases for professionals who are not AI specialists.
- Google published an update on how it is combatting AI scams, covering improved scam detection in its products, support for new legislation, and consumer awareness work, since scammers are increasingly using generative AI to impersonate people and create convincing fake content.
- A Towards Data Science article demonstrates that vision-capable LLMs can be used as PDF parsers, extracting meaning from charts, diagrams, and figures, not just text. This is useful for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems that need to handle messy, real-world documents.

## Why It Matters

- Free, structured AI upskilling from a major vendor gives RP lecturers and students a low-cost route to build practical AI literacy that maps to real workplace tasks, useful for staff development and student self-learning.
- AI scam awareness is directly relevant for diploma students. They are both potential targets and future creators of digital content, and need to recognise voice clones, fake images, phishing, and impersonation generated by AI.
- Vision LLMs that read charts and diagrams change what students can do with PDFs. Lab manuals, datasheets, infographics, and research papers become more accessible for summarisation, study aids, and assistive learning, but also raise questions about accuracy and over-reliance.

## Try This Today

- Spend 10 minutes browsing the new OpenAI Academy "Applying AI at Work" course list and pick one short module relevant to your module or diploma area to try this week.
- Take a PDF that contains a chart or diagram (e.g. a lecture slide export or a lab handout) and upload it to a vision-capable chatbot. Ask it to describe the chart and extract the key data points, then check whether the numbers are correct.
- Run a quick scam-spotting drill: paste a suspicious-looking message or describe a deepfake scenario to an AI assistant and ask it to list the red flags. Compare with Google's published advice on AI scams.

## Teaching Angle

- Use the OpenAI Academy courses as optional pre-class preparation or as a flipped-learning resource, then run a 15-minute classroom discussion on which AI work tasks students see as realistic in their future jobs.
- Run a short "spot the AI scam" activity in tutorial: show examples of AI-generated phishing messages, voice clone scenarios, or fake images, and ask students to identify clues and propose verification steps. Tie this to digital citizenship and cybersecurity modules.
- Demonstrate a Vision LLM reading a chart from a course PDF in front of the class. Ask students to verify the output against the original, and discuss when this is safe to rely on (study aid) versus risky (assessment answers, technical reports).

## Links

- [New OpenAI Academy courses for the next era of work](https://openai.com/index/academy-courses-applying-ai-at-work)
- [How we're combatting AI scams with security, legislation and more](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/safety-security/combatting-ai-scams/)
- [Vision LLMs are PDF Parsers Too: Reading Charts and Diagrams for RAG](https://towardsdatascience.com/vision-llms-are-pdf-parsers-too-reading-charts-and-diagrams-for-rag/)
